meta.subtitle: Stronger, steadier blood sugar and more energy — built around a desk job, home workouts and two gym days a week. FICTIONAL EXAMPLE used to test the workbook builder.

overview.schedule_title: Your week — how it builds up

schedule.session: Full body B (gym) or Busy Day

overview.schedule_note: Busy week? Two Busy Day sessions plus your walks still count as a good week. Days can move — just avoid hard sessions on back-to-back days.
priorities: 1. Do your 2–3 strength sessions — on busy days, the 15-minute Busy Day version counts.
2. Walk 10–15 minutes after your two biggest meals.
3. A protein food at every meal (egg, dal, paneer, curd, chana, sprouts).
4. Fill the Daily Check-in each evening — rough is fine.
expectations: Stronger: more reps or harder versions of squats, push-ups and rows by week 4.
Weight usually trends down 0.25–0.5 kg a week on average, with ups and downs day to day. We judge the weekly average plus waist, not one weigh-in.
Exercise can't burn fat from one spot. Overall strength training, steps and food habits change body shape over time.
listen_to_body: Mild muscle soreness for 1–2 days is normal. Sharp pain or pain that changes how you move is not — stop that exercise and tell your coach.
Shaky, sweaty or light-headed during training → stop, sit, have a small snack, and tell your coach.
Stop and get medical help for chest pain or pressure, fainting, unusual breathlessness or a sudden severe headache.
overview.equipment: Home: two 5 kg dumbbells, a sturdy chair, a yoga mat. Gym (Wed/Sat): standard machines and dumbbells.

sessions.title: Full Body A — Home
sessions.subtitle: Squat, push, pull, hinge and core with two 5 kg dumbbells and a chair.
sessions.purpose: Home full-body session (Mon, and Fri from week 3)
info: Build leg, back and pushing strength with simple moves you can progress at home.
About 35–40 minutes including warm-up and cool-down.
March on the spot 2 min · arm circles ×10 each way · cat-cow ×6 · glute bridge ×8 · squat to chair ×6.
Stop each set with 2–3 good reps left (RPE about 7). Weeks 1–2: 3–4 reps left.
Child's pose 30 s · hip-flexor stretch 30 s each side · slow breathing 1 min.

blocks.label: HOME VERSION  ·  two 5 kg dumbbells, chair, mat

exercises.name: Squat to chair
exercises.cues: Feet hip-width, sit back slowly until you touch the chair, stand tall. Knees follow toes.

exercises.name: Incline push-up (counter or sofa edge)
exercises.cues: Hands on a sturdy edge, body straight head to heels, chest to the edge, push away.
exercises.if_bothers: Hands slightly wider; stop if a shoulder pinches

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
exercises.cues: Hand and knee on a chair, pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close, lower slowly.
exercises.easier: Both feet on floor, hand on chair

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
exercises.cues: Soft knees, push hips back with a flat back, dumbbells slide down the thighs, stand tall squeezing glutes.
exercises.if_bothers: Shorter range; skip if lower back complains

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.cues: On your back, knees over hips, lower back gently on the floor. Lower opposite arm and leg slowly, switch.
exercises.if_bothers: Smaller range if your back arches

sessions.footer: Tick the session on your Daily Check-in.

sessions.title: Full Body B — Gym
sessions.subtitle: Machines and dumbbells: same movement patterns, a little more load.
info: Stop each set with 2–3 good reps left. Increase weight only when all sets reach the top of the range.

exercises.name: Box squat
exercises.cues: Sit back to a box, stand tall pushing through the whole foot.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.cues: Sit tall, pull the bar to your upper chest, shoulders down.

exercises.name: Chest press machine
exercises.cues: Handles at mid-chest, press forward, return slowly.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl machine
exercises.cues: Pad above the heels, curl down slowly, control back up.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
exercises.cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, walk tall, shoulders down, slow steps.

sessions.title: Mobility + Walk
sessions.subtitle: Tuesday and Thursday: loosen hips, back and shoulders after desk hours, then walk.
info: 15–20 minutes on the mat, then a 20–30 minute walk — ideally after a meal.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
exercises.cues: On hands and knees, round then gently arch your back with your breath.

exercises.name: Thread the needle
exercises.cues: Slide one arm under your body, turning the upper back. Return.

exercises.name: Child's pose
exercises.cues: Sit back towards your heels, arms forward, relax.

sessions.title: Busy Day — 15 Minutes
sessions.subtitle: When a full session won't fit. It counts.
info: 2-minute march, then the 4 moves back to back. Rest 60 s. 2–3 rounds.

progression.title: Progression — weeks 1 to 12
progression.subtitle: Main exercises stay the same so progress is visible. They get harder one small step at a time.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Foundation
phases.aim: Learn the moves, build the routine

phases.name: Phase 3 — Strength
phases.aim: Progress load on the main lifts
phases.sets_effort: 3 sets · 1–3 reps left on main lifts

sections.title: How an exercise gets harder — double progression
bullets: 1. Each exercise has a rep range, e.g. 8–12. Start at the bottom.
2. Add reps until ALL sets reach the top of the range with good form and 2–3 reps left.
3. Do that in two sessions in a row → move up one step (a bit more weight or the next harder version). Reps drop back to the bottom of the range.
4. Bad week or symptoms? Stay where you are, or step back. That's normal progress.

sections.title: Ready to progress? All must be true

rows: All sets reach the top of the range
2–3 good reps left at the end of each set
Back to normal by the next day or two

sections.title: Lighter weeks
bullets: Take a lighter week (one set fewer, same exercises) after illness, poor sleep for several days, travel, or if everything feels heavy.

nutrition.title: Nutrition — your usual food, a little more protein
nutrition.subtitle: Built on home-cooked meals. No food bans. Numbers are estimates — recipes and portions change them.

targets.why: Keeps you full and protects muscle while losing fat (about 1.25 g per kg). The sample week below averages about this.
A gentle deficit from your estimated maintenance. Only if you choose to track — the plate guide works without counting.

targets.target: Half your plate at lunch and dinner
targets.why: Fibre and volume; eat them first, then roti/rice — helps after-meal blood sugar.
More on training and hot days. Pale-yellow urine is a good sign.

guides: ½ plate vegetables · ¼ plate protein (dal, rajma, chole, egg, paneer, curd) · ¼ plate rice or roti (about 1 cup cooked rice or 2 medium roti).
1 katori ≈ 150 ml · 1 cup cooked rice ≈ 150 g · 1 tsp oil/ghee ≈ 45 kcal · 1 tbsp ≈ 120 kcal.
Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how far apart to keep it from tea/coffee, food and any calcium or iron supplement.

menu.note: Rotate freely. Days land within about 10 g of each other — that's fine. Protein values are estimates.

sections.title: Keep it flexible
bullets: No food is banned. Sweets and snacks can fit — a planned portion, enjoyed.
Eating out: pick the protein dish first, enjoy the meal, and go back to normal at the next meal — no skipping to 'make up'.
Walk 10–15 minutes after your two biggest meals.

intro: Food first: most of your needs are covered by the meals above.
Everything below is optional and was chosen for your profile. Start one thing at a time so we can tell what helps.

items.name: Methi (fenugreek) seed water
items.why_for_you: Your HbA1c was in the prediabetes range. Fenugreek has modest evidence for lowering blood sugar.
items.how: 1 tsp seeds soaked overnight in a glass of water; drink in the morning (seeds can be chewed). Keep it at least an hour away from your thyroid tablet unless your doctor says otherwise.
items.cautions: Can add to the effect of blood-sugar medicines (risk of going too low). Avoid in pregnancy. Can cause gas or loose stools. Allergy possible if allergic to peanuts/chickpeas. Check with your doctor if you take blood thinners.
items.alternative: 10–15 min walk after meals (stronger evidence for after-meal blood sugar)

items.name: Vitamin D3
items.why_for_you: Low vitamin D is common in India, especially with indoor work.
items.how: Only after a blood test or your doctor's advice; dose depends on the result.
items.cautions: Don't self-dose high amounts. Check with your doctor if you have kidney stones or kidney disease.
items.alternative: Test first; morning sunlight on arms and face

not_recommended.name: Apple cider vinegar shots
not_recommended.why: Small effect on after-meal blood sugar at best; can worsen acidity and wear tooth enamel. The after-meal walk does the same job better for you.

habits.why: Lowers after-meal blood sugar and adds steps

habits.what: Egg, dal, paneer, curd, chana or sprouts with each meal
Screens away 30 min before bed, same wake time daily
habits.why: Short sleep makes hunger and cravings louder

recovery: Aim for 7–8 hours. Log your hours for 2–3 weeks before we change anything.
Last tea/coffee by about 2 pm if sleep is a problem.
Gentle walking or stretching is fine; never required.

sections.title: Busy or difficult week — the minimum plan
bullets: Two Busy Day sessions + daily after-meal walks = a successful week.
Missed a day? Just do the next planned session — no doubling up.

evidence.notes: Light walking after meals lowered post-prandial glucose vs prolonged sitting.
